A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenHOI. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRAB and ARCTIC evaluations, cross-dataset H2O results, component ablations, guidance sensitivity and qualitative interaction sequences.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds physical-realism evaluations, affordance-token and window-size ablations, affordance visualizations and statistical comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated targets of the refinement losses in Equations 9–10 from closest object surfaces to closest affordance regions, reinforced by Appendix E.1. The backbone, coarse-to-fine training, multi-token grounding and diffusion framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same identified affordance-training data, GRAB and ARCTIC evaluations, and cross-dataset H2O testing. The new analyses and visual examples concern the existing HOI and affordance-grounding tasks; no distinct additional dataset or application domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding GRAB, ARCTIC and H2O comparisons retain MDM, TM2T, MotionGPT and Text2HOI; qualitative comparisons retain MDM and Text2HOI. The added physical-realism evaluation reuses Text2HOI. HOIGPT is explicitly described as unavailable for evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds Physical Realism and IV metrics and a GRAB motion-window sweep over sizes 1, 3, 5, 10 and 20. Its revised smoothness summary matches the size-5 setting. Section 4.1 also changes the annotation-model description from LLM to MLLM, although the appendix still says LLM. Existing splits and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds physical-refinement ablation under physical metrics, single-versus-multiple affordance-token ablation, window-size sensitivity, affordance-grounding visualizations and explicit failure analysis. These substantially extend component validation. The ARCTIC component ablation and H2O generalization test already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Beyond the existing plus/minus reporting, Appendix C.9 and Table A11 introduce systematic paired two-sample t-tests across component ablations, five repetitions of each test, mean p-values and a 0.05 threshold. This adds a statistical assessment procedure; it does not establish an increase in training runs or disclose their seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds physical-realism, refinement, token-configuration, window-size and significance results. For example, Table A2 reports seen-object physical realism of 0.93 for OpenHOI versus 0.87 for Text2HOI. GRAB SmoothRate summaries change from 4.77/5.26 to 2.98/3.70 for seen/unseen objects; Table A10 associates these pairs with window sizes 1 and 5, respectively, so this is not an established same-setting gain. Main benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The target-point definitions accompanying Equations 9–10 change from nearest object surfaces to nearest affordance regions, altering the mathematical meaning of those objectives despite unchanged algebra. The diffusion derivations, ELBO argument and SmoothRate definition are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: first open-world HOI synthesis, generalization to unseen objects and open-vocabulary instructions, long-horizon generation, and superior benchmark performance. Additional evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's general dynamics and hierarchical-task limitations, Section 4.5 adds failure to select a specified cabinet and degradation beyond three actions or 450 frames, with proposed explanations. Appendix E expands the affordance mechanism discussion, identifies ShapeLLM's missing part-level supervision, and discusses robotics transfer and inference-speed constraints.

D1.justification: v2 expands metric descriptions and supplies a GitHub link. Appendix D replaces the promise to release code and data upon acceptance with a promise to release code soon, without retaining the explicit data-release commitment. The PDFs do not establish actual repository availability. Core implementation and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including DAG, seamless motion composition, THOR, AffordDP and GraspXL, extending context for affordances, motion composition and robotics. The principal positioning against text-driven HOI and perception-only MLLM approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. v2 makes localized terminology and metric-explanation edits, adds a failure-analysis subsection and discussion appendix, reorganizes appendix subsections, and updates the venue footer. There is no extensive rewrite of the existing paper.

P2.justification: The appendix gains an affordance-map figure and new tables presenting physical realism, refinement and token ablations, window sensitivity and p-values. The existing ARCTIC ablation moves from Table A5 to main-text Table 5, and existing qualitative figures are redistributed and renumbered. Main motivation, pipeline and sequence figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added component and window-size analyses strengthen validation, while concrete failure boundaries make the generalization claims easier to assess. These are useful but limited gains: the main benchmark evidence is unchanged, the new physical metrics lack definitions and clear dataset attribution, and averaging repeated-test p-values is insufficiently explained. The revision improves transparency and supporting evidence without establishing a substantial overall increase in rigor.
